record.paper_title: Similarity: generalizations, applications and open problems
record.original_question: For partial differential equation models whose ultimate evolution is long-time behavior or behavior close to a finite-time singularity, what role do quasi-self-similar solutions, meaning solutions that satisfy the governing equations asymptotically rather than exactly, play in describing that evolution, and how should their analysis combine similarity methods, dynamical-systems methods, perturbation methods, and numerical methods?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a partial differential equation (or system of PDEs) of the form $\partial_t u = F(u, \nabla u, \nabla^2 u, \dots)$ on a spatial domain $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, where $F$ is invariant (or asymptotically invariant) under a one-parameter scaling group $u(x,t) \mapsto \lambda^{\alpha} u(\lambda x, \lambda^{\beta} t)$ for suitable exponents $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$. A solution $u(x,t)$ is called self-similar if it is exactly invariant under this group, i.e. it has the form $u(x,t) = (T-t)^{-\alpha/\beta} U\bigl(x/(T-t)^{1/\beta}\bigr)$ (for finite-time singular evolutions, with blow-up time $T < \infty$) or $u(x,t) = t^{-\alpha/\beta} U(x/t^{1/\beta})$ (for long-time evolutions). A solution is called quasi-self-similar if it satisfies the governing equations only asymptotically, in the sense that, after passing to similarity variables $\xi = x/(T-t)^{1/\beta}$, $\tau = -\log(T-t)$ (or analogous variables for long-time behaviour), the rescaled profile $U(\xi,\tau)$ converges as $\tau \to \infty$ to a profile $U_\infty(\xi)$ which solves the reduced (scaling-invariant) profile equation, while $U(\xi,\tau)$ itself does not exactly solve the profile equation at finite $\tau$.

Develop a rigorous framework that:
(a) characterizes when quasi-self-similar solutions exist and govern the long-time behaviour or the behaviour close to a finite-time singularity for solutions of such PDEs;
(b) determines their stability under the rescaled flow in similarity variables, by combining:
   (i) similarity (scaling) reductions to a profile equation,
   (ii) dynamical-systems analysis of the rescaled flow (fixed points, invariant manifolds, center manifolds, spectral analysis of the linearization about $U_\infty$),
   (iii) perturbative asymptotic expansions in $1/\tau$ or other small parameters capturing the deviation from exact self-similarity,
   (iv) numerical continuation and time-marching schemes in similarity variables to detect and validate $U_\infty$;
(c) proves, in a class of model PDEs of physical interest (for example semilinear heat equations, nonlinear Schrödinger equations, geometric flows, or compressible Euler/Navier–Stokes equations), that the ultimate evolution is described by a quasi-self-similar profile when no exact self-similar solution with the required regularity and stability exists.

Formulate and prove such characterization, stability, and selection results, or exhibit counterexamples.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is broad and programmatic, asking for a general theory of quasi-self-similar (asymptotically self-similar) solutions across PDE models. Such a unified theory does not exist; while individual instances (e.g. semilinear heat equations, NLS blow-up, Euler/Navier–Stokes singularities) have been treated with combinations of similarity, dynamical-systems, perturbative, and numerical methods, the overall program remains active and open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Similarity: generalizations, applications and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the role of quasi-self-similar solutions in ultimate evolution and lists open problems.
